title: 节约用水
subtitle: 从原因到对策
essay: One of the worrying trends in modern society is **the decreasing availability of drinkable water**.
This occurs for several reasons, the foremost of which are increasing water pollution and **water wastage**.
Concerted efforts from governments and individuals should be made to remedy this alarming situation.
The main cause of insufficient drinkable water is **growing water pollution**.
As the population has dramatically increased over the past decades, there is an increasing need for essential items **such as food and clothing**.
**The production of these items can** pollute **water sources** by releasing toxic chemicals or pesticides into the waterways, reducing the total amount of **water safe to drink**.
Apart from water pollution, this problem is also being exacerbated by **wasteful daily habits**; for example, people may brush their teeth without turning off the tap.
The sheer size of the population makes such minor **acts of waste** a serious problem, **putting further pressure on freshwater supplies**.
What steps can governments and **individuals** take to halt and reverse the trend?
This requires the government to impose regulations governing industrial processes to increase the efficiency of water use **and impose sanctions on water polluters**.
For example, **wastewater from food and clothing production should be treated to** meet wastewater discharge standards.
Individuals can also help to deal with **this shortage** by recycling water or **avoiding waste** in their daily lives.
For example, the water used for washing **vegetables could be reused to water plants**; people could turn off the tap while brushing their teeth.
In conclusion, **growing** water pollution and **wastage** have given rise to **a shortage of drinkable water**.
Efforts should be made to change the status quo, including **enforcing regulations and reducing waste in daily life**.
Otherwise, this disturbing trend **could be** a recipe for disaster.
paragraphLabels: 引言 · 预告原因与对策
outline: 开头：安全饮用水越来越少 → 污染与浪费是两项主要原因 → 政府和个人共同应对。
原因段：人口增长 → 食品与衣物需求增加 → 生产释放污染物 → 可安全饮用的水减少；个人浪费量小 → 人口规模放大累积 → 淡水供应进一步承压。
措施段：工业流程规定与污染处罚 → 提高效率、约束排污；废水处理达标 → 回应生产污染；重复利用水与刷牙关水 → 回应日常浪费。
结尾：重申两项原因与对应措施 → 不处理可能造成严重后果。

steps.title: 审题与全文路线
steps.copy: 题目问原因和措施，文章因此采用四段组织。开头同时预告污染、浪费，以及政府、个人两个行动主体。不要把它写成只讨论后果的文章。
steps.label: 全文路线
steps.tip: 两问分别是 Why 和 What can be done。读完时，要能给每项原因找到对应措施。

steps.title: 开头的名词结构
steps.copy: 核心是 availability；decreasing 说明可获得程度下降，of drinkable water 限定对象。它避免原文 worrying trends 后重复 downward trend。饮用水可获得量下降不等于地球上的水总量下降。
steps.label: 名词短语拆解
steps.tip: 修的是重复与搭配：保留 One of the worrying trends 的正式开头，不再嵌套 a downward trend。

steps.title: 原因排序与关系从句
steps.copy: which 指 several reasons；the foremost of which 从原因中提取最主要的项。本句列两项，所以用 are。Concerted efforts 预告共同应对，正文分别说明谁做什么。
steps.label: 关系从句拆解
steps.tip: remedy 直接接宾语：remedy this alarming situation，不加 to。Concerted efforts from 可理解；by 更常用来明确行动者。本课保留修订版。

steps.title: 污染链与指代
steps.copy: As 引出背景原因；an increasing need for 后接物品 food and clothing。these items 回指物品，真正排污的主语是 The production，而非食品和衣物自己。can 为污染机制保留条件。
steps.label: 污染的中间机制
steps.tip: 原文 Both 的对象容易模糊。The production of these items 把指代和真正发生的活动一起写清楚。

steps.title: 一个长句如何推进因果
steps.copy: 主干是“生产能污染水源”；by releasing 是方式；reducing 表示前述污染造成的结果。中文可拆成几步理解，英文仍保留原有长句。toxic chemicals or pesticides 描述可能的污染物，不表示两个互斥类别。
steps.label: 长句的三个层次
parts: The production … can pollute water sources
主干：什么活动影响什么
结果：前述污染带来什么变化
steps.tip: 长句的价值来自层次清晰。by + V-ing 写方式，逗号后的 V-ing 在此概括结果。

steps.title: 浪费的规模效应
steps.copy: Apart from 补充第二项原因；is being exacerbated by 是进行时被动，表示已有短缺正在被加剧。sheer size 强调人口规模本身，不是再次说人口增长。minor acts → population scale → pressure 是这部分的核心。
steps.label: 规模放大效应
steps.tip: exacerbate 是“使已有问题更严重”；give rise to 是“引发某种结果”。两者不能只当高级近义词来替换。

steps.title: 政府措施回应污染
steps.copy: This requires the government to 后并列两个动作 impose… and impose…；governing 修饰 regulations，相当于 that govern。impose 突出施加规定，enforce 突出确保遵守。处理废水至达标，是对前面生产污染的直接回应；排放处理与提高效率分别对应不同机制。
steps.label: 原因与措施对应
pairs: 工业流程监管 + 排污处罚 + 废水处理
steps.tip: impose regulations：施加规定；enforce regulations：确保执行。impose sanctions on + 受罚主体，结构要完整。

steps.title: 个人措施回应浪费
steps.copy: by 后的 recycling 与 avoiding 平行。关水龙头直接回应前文刷牙浪费；再利用展示减少额外用水的场景。could 表示可行选择，不把这个例子推广为所有废水都适合灌溉。
steps.label: 让例子回应原因
pairs: 适当重复利用用过的水
steps.tip: the water used for washing vegetables 中的 used 是过去分词，修饰 water；could be reused 是主句被动结构。

steps.title: 结论不另起论点
steps.copy: give rise to 后接名词短语 a shortage，说明结果形成；它与 exacerbate 的“加剧已有问题”不同。结尾回收污染、浪费、执行规定与个人行动。a recipe for disaster 是较强的风险比喻，could 保留可能性，但仍应理解其正式写作中的语气。
steps.label: 结论的闭环
chain: 执行规定 + 减少浪费
steps.tip: could be 保留可能性；a recipe for disaster 的风险语气仍然很强。理解语域后再迁移，不必每篇结尾都用。

steps.title: 本篇搭配：从理解到迁移
steps.copy: 优先记住完整的句法槽位和论证作用。以下例句均为自拟跨话题示范。
steps.label: 搭配迁移

steps.title: 空白回忆：把论证写出来
steps.copy: 先收起提示，用中文还原推理，再把熟悉的英文句架写出来。完成后再展开参考答案。
steps.label: 主动回忆

collocations.usage: 从前述多项原因挑出主要项；which 有明确的复数先行词，后列两项用 are
collocations.example: This problem has several causes, the foremost of which are high rents and low wages.

collocations.phrase: an increasing need for essential items
collocations.usage: need for + N，表达需求增长
collocations.example: An ageing population can create an increasing need for accessible housing.

collocations.usage: release + 排放物 + into + 接收环境，交代污染机制
collocations.example: Factories may release harmful gases into the atmosphere.

collocations.phrase: be exacerbated by wasteful daily habits
collocations.source: 熟悉（讲义）句型／校正搭配
collocations.usage: be exacerbated by + N/V-ing，已有问题被加剧
collocations.example: Traffic congestion can be exacerbated by unreliable bus services.

collocations.phrase: the sheer size of the population
collocations.usage: the sheer size of + N，规模放大小影响
collocations.example: The sheer size of the student population makes small improvements to school meals significant.

collocations.usage: impose regulations + governing N，明确规定管理对象
collocations.example: Governments could impose regulations governing the collection of personal data.

collocations.usage: impose sanctions on + 受罚主体，交代违规后果
collocations.example: Authorities could impose sanctions on companies that breach safety rules.

collocations.phrase: give rise to a shortage of drinkable water
collocations.source: 熟悉（讲义）句型／校正宾语
collocations.usage: give rise to + N，指出形成的结果；to 是介词
collocations.example: A shortage of affordable homes can give rise to longer commutes.

questions: 饮用水短缺的两个原因是什么？生产需求如何一步步影响可安全饮用的水？
为什么一个人刷牙浪费的少量水，也能支持全文的原因分析？
污染和浪费分别由什么措施回应？谁负责执行？
补全：This problem is also being ______ by ______.
补全：Governments should impose regulations ______ industrial processes and impose sanctions ______ water polluters.
transfer: 迁移：换到塑料包装，先写“单次用量小 → 消费人数多 → 总量可观”，再用两三句英文展开。
question: The amount of drinkable water for people is decreasing. Why is this? What can be done?
type: 原因与措施 · 四段结构
position: 污染与浪费造成短缺；政府和个人的措施分别回应这两项原因。
answers: 两项原因是污染与浪费。人口增长 → 食品和衣物需求增加 → 生产可能把化学品或农药排入水道 → 可安全饮用的水减少。
单次行为的浪费虽然少，但人口规模让重复行为累积成大消耗，从而进一步增加淡水供应压力。sheer size 强调规模，不是增长速度。
政府监管工业流程、处罚污染者并要求废水处理达标，回应污染；个人刷牙关水和适当重复利用水，回应浪费。
This problem is also being exacerbated by wasteful daily habits. be exacerbated by + 原因。
governing；on。governing industrial processes 修饰 regulations；impose sanctions on water polluters 明确处罚对象。
transferAnswer: The sheer number of daily purchases means that even small amounts of packaging can add up to substantial waste. Individuals could reduce unnecessary packaging by choosing products with reusable containers.

title: 用水限制
subtitle: 从双方观点到合理边界
essay: The **importance of water resources is beyond doubt**; however, opinions differ as to how water should be used.
Some people think individuals have the right to use it freely, whereas others insist that it should be stringently controlled by governments for sustainable development.
**In my view, governments should regulate excessive consumption while protecting basic water needs.**
The argument in favour of giving priority to individuals' needs is that **water is a shared natural resource**.
**From this perspective,** no one individual or organization can lay **exclusive** claim to **it**; therefore, everyone is born with the right to use **it** freely.

**Supporters therefore believe that people should be free to use water to meet their needs**, be it for domestic use or commercial purposes, as long as they pay for the costs involved in the treatment and transport of fresh water.
Others, however, highlight the urgent need for **governments** to impose regulations on water usage.
**Despite knowing** that water is finite, individuals still waste water in their daily **lives** (e.g., leaving the kitchen without turning off the tap).

**Such waste may seem negligible**; nonetheless, the sheer size of the population **means that these habits can ultimately contribute to** the depletion of fresh water, a problem **that could affect both current and future generations**.
Governments, as the **protectors of the public interest**, should **adopt policies** to halt such a worrying trend.
Although individuals have **a** prima facie right **to use water**, **concern for future generations** justifies **measures** to limit **excessive** water usage.

Tiered water rates, for example, are designed to **charge lower rates for water used to meet basic needs and higher rates for consumption above this level, providing an incentive to reduce excessive use**.
**Therefore**, water usage **can be regulated without restricting access to water for basic needs**, while slowing down **the depletion of freshwater resources**.
In conclusion, **individuals should enjoy the right to meet their basic water needs, while governments should regulate excessive consumption.**
**Tiered water rates offer a way to balance these aims while slowing down the depletion of fresh water.**
paragraphLabels: 引言 · 双方与个人立场
观点 A · 自由使用
观点 B · 政府监管
我的判断 · 阶梯水价
结论 · 呼应全文立场
outline: 开头：水很重要 → 自由使用与政府管控存在分歧 → 我的立场是保障基本需求、规制过量消费。
支持自由使用：共享自然资源 → 支持者认为个人有使用权 → 支付处理运输成本后应能满足需求。
支持监管：明知水有限仍浪费 → 单次量小但人口规模大 → 可能造成资源耗减 → 当代和后代的公共利益需要保护。
我的判断：承认初步使用权 → 对后代的关切支持合理限制 → 基本用量低费率、超额用量高费率 → 通过价格激励减少过量消费，并保护基本需求。
结尾：重申基本用水权与过量消费监管 → 阶梯水价兼顾二者并减缓耗减。

steps.title: 开头直接给出判断
steps.copy: 双边讨论不等于作者没有立场。while protecting 压缩了同时保护的动作，主语仍是 governments。basic 与 excessive 划定全文的范围，后面的政策与结论都应沿用这条界线。
steps.label: 全文的范围界线
steps.tip: while protecting 的行动者仍是 governments。开头已经给出判断，结尾应回到同一条界线。

steps.title: 公平呈现自由使用方
steps.copy: 本段展示支持者的理由。From this perspective 与 Supporters therefore believe 确保读者知道这是该方推理，不是作者直接宣布无限用水权。shared resource → no exclusive claim → free use 是其推理路径，但公共资源不自动推导无限使用。
steps.label: 这一方如何推理
steps.tip: From this perspective 和 Supporters therefore believe 负责标明观点归属。呈现一个理由，不代表作者已证明它的全部结论。

steps.title: 指代与正式结构
steps.copy: it 回指 water，不能在 water 与 water resources 间随意变换代词单复数。be it A or B 是正式的列举结构，domestic 指家庭用途。as long as 表示条件，后接完整从句；这里的条件是支付处理运输成本。
steps.label: 正式长句的层次
parts: 回指 water，单数 / 不可数对象
be it for A or B
无论是 A 用途还是 B 用途
as long as + 完整从句
条件：支付处理和运输成本
steps.tip: domestic 在此是“家庭的”；lay claim to 表示主张拥有，并不表示主张已经被法律认可。

steps.title: 为什么监管方不只是反对自由
steps.copy: Others, however 转向另一方，后面要解释理由。Despite 是介词，后接 knowing；其隐含主语与主句 individuals 一致。知道资源有限却仍浪费构成让步，不能写 Despite people know。
steps.label: 让步结构
parts: Despite knowing that water is finite
steps.tip: 不要把 despite 当连词接 people know。可比较 although people know，但本课保留修订版 Despite knowing。

steps.title: 指代清楚的累积论证
steps.copy: Such waste 回指上一句的浪费行为；these habits 回指不关水龙头等习惯。may seem 说明单次浪费看起来很小，nonetheless 转向人口累积后的结果；can ultimately contribute to 是“可能促成”，没有把它写成唯一原因。
steps.label: 从微小到不可忽略
steps.tip: Such waste 回指浪费；these habits 回指造成浪费的日常习惯。negligible 的表面印象由 nonetheless 后的规模论证修正。

steps.title: 结果的范围与责任主体
steps.copy: a problem 概括前述资源耗减；that 修饰 problem。could 避免必然预测，both current and future 不再声称当前完全不受影响。公共利益解释政府为什么应行动，adopt policies 则引向后面的具体方案。
steps.label: 用词控制结论强度
parts: that 修饰 problem；could 保留可能性
当代与后代，不把影响推迟到未来
解释政府应行动的公共责任
steps.tip: 政府为什么应该行动，与政策怎样有效，是两步论证。下一段需要把 adopt policies 变成具体方案。

steps.title: 让步不等于取消权利
steps.copy: Although 从句承认初步权利，主句给出合理限制的依据。prima facie 意为初步成立、表面看来成立，有法律语域色彩，不能译成绝对不可限制。justify + N/V-ing 是“提供合理理由”，不是证明政策必然有效。to limit 修饰 measures，且限制对象明确为 excessive usage。
steps.label: 让步 → 理由 → 有限度判断
steps.tip: prima facie 有法律语域色彩，意为初步成立；justify + 名词 / V-ing 提供合理理由，不等于证明措施必定有效。

steps.title: 拆开阶梯水价的政策长句
steps.copy: 主干为 rates are designed to charge；lower rates 与 higher rates 对应不同用量层级。above this level 的 this level 指满足基本需求的用量水平，不指价格高低。providing 给出成本变化带来的激励：额外用水成本更高 → 有动力减少超额消费。它不是对所有用水统一涨价，也不保证所有人都节约。
steps.label: 价格怎样改变行为
pairs: 较低费率 → 保护基本需求
较高费率 → 提供减少超量用水的激励
steps.tip: this level 指基本需求对应的用量水平。providing an incentive 是前述收费设计产生的激励，不是人人都会响应的保证。

steps.title: 把政策回扣到两项目标
steps.copy: without + V-ing 说明政策边界，while slowing down 说明同时追求的资源结果。保护基本需求是这套方案的设计目标；本文没有检验现实收费实施的全部条件。讲解聚焦作者怎样使政策与立场对应。
steps.label: 政策回扣两项目标
parts: 交代基本需求的保护边界
同时追求减缓资源耗减
steps.tip: without + V-ing；access to + 名词。本文讨论方案的设计逻辑，不承诺任何实际水价安排都自动保障可负担性。

steps.title: 结论与全文一致
steps.copy: 第一分句重申 basic needs，第二分句重申 excessive consumption，最后再提 tiered rates。它回应开头与个人观点段，不再回到“维持现状、任意用水、只管工业”的旧结论。
steps.label: 开头与结尾对照
pairs: 结尾：right to meet their basic water needs
steps.tip: 原结尾的“任意用水 + 只管工业”没有回应居民阶梯水价。修订版统一了对象、范围和工具。

steps.copy: 优先记住完整的句法槽位和论证作用。以下例句均为自拟跨话题示范。
steps.label: 搭配迁移

steps.title: 空白回忆：把论证写出来
steps.copy: 先收起提示，用中文还原推理，再把熟悉的英文句架写出来。完成后再展开参考答案。

collocations.phrase: opinions differ as to how water should be used
collocations.usage: as to + 疑问从句，说明分歧对象；嵌入问句用陈述语序
collocations.example: Opinions differ as to how public transport should be funded.

collocations.phrase: The argument in favour of giving priority to individuals' needs is that…
collocations.usage: in favour of + N/V-ing；give priority to + N/V-ing；is that 后完整从句
collocations.example: The argument in favour of giving priority to practical training is that students can develop job-related skills.

collocations.source: 熟悉（讲义）句型／通用补充限定词
collocations.usage: lay claim to + N，主张拥有；exclusive 表示排他
collocations.example: No single department should lay exclusive claim to shared research facilities.

collocations.phrase: highlight the urgent need for governments to impose regulations
collocations.usage: highlight + N；need for sb to do，明确行动主体
collocations.example: This case highlights the urgent need for schools to improve data protection.

collocations.phrase: contribute to the depletion of fresh water
collocations.source: 熟悉（通用搭配库）／熟悉（讲义）名词
collocations.usage: contribute to + N/V-ing；depletion of + 资源，表达促成耗减
collocations.example: Excessive household energy use can contribute to the depletion of finite fuel resources.

collocations.phrase: concern for future generations justifies measures to limit…
collocations.usage: concern for + 关切对象；justify + N；measures to do，给出限制的理由
collocations.example: Concern for children's privacy justifies measures to limit unnecessary data collection.

collocations.phrase: providing an incentive to reduce excessive use
collocations.source: 熟悉（讲义）句型／校正语境
collocations.usage: provide an incentive to do；也可 provide an incentive for sb to do
collocations.example: Affordable training can provide an incentive for employees to update their skills.

collocations.phrase: without restricting access to water for basic needs
collocations.source: 熟悉（讲义）access to／通用补充组合
collocations.usage: without + V-ing；access to + N，说明措施应保护的边界
collocations.example: Libraries could reduce operating costs without restricting access to essential learning resources.

questions: 自由使用方为什么认为付费后应能满足需求？哪些措辞说明这是支持者的观点？
为什么 negligible 之后还能讨论 depletion？中间不能省略哪一步？
阶梯水价如何区分基本需求与过量消费？它通过什么机制改变行为？

question: Some people think they have the right to use as much water as they want, while others think the government should control the use of freshwater strictly, as it is limited. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
questionNote: 题干按附件原意规范拼写与语法；范文保持用户提供的修订版。
type: 双边讨论 + 个人观点 · 五段结构
position: 保障基本用水，同时规制过量消费；用阶梯水价把两个目标结合起来。
answers: 支持者从共享自然资源出发，反对排他占有，并主张付清处理运输成本后自由满足需求。From this perspective 和 Supporters therefore believe 标明这是支持者的观点。
必须补上人口规模带来的累积效应。单次浪费看似 negligible，并不意味着大量重复行为的总影响也可忽略。
基本用量采用较低费率，超出基本需求水平的用量采用较高费率。额外用水成本更高 → 为减少过量消费提供激励，同时保护基本需求。
to use；for；measures。have a right to do；concern for + 对象；justify + 名词，measures to limit … 说明措施目的。
参考：Individuals should enjoy the right to meet their basic water needs, while governments should regulate excessive consumption. Tiered water rates offer a way to balance these aims.
transferAnswer: Although people should be able to make essential journeys, concern for congestion may justify measures to limit unnecessary driving at peak times. Higher charges for additional car journeys could provide an incentive to use public transport where suitable services are available.
